newsitem.title: GERMANY: German general to be Chief of Staff in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: German general to be Chief of Staff in Bosnia.

text.p: A German major-general will be chief of staff for NATO's follow-on force in Bosnia, the German defence ministry said on Sunday.

The major-general, whose name has not been released by the ministry, will take up his post in the New Year in the Sarajevo headquarters of the Stabilisation Force (SFOR), which is due to replace the peace Implementation Force on December 20.

Germany's role in any peacekeeping operation in the Balkans has long been a controversial issue, both in domestic political terms and internationally because of Nazi Germany's World War Two occupation and its vicious fight against local partisans.
He will serve under U.S. General William Crouch, who took control of all NATO-led peace forces in Bosnia in November.
Defence Minister Volker Ruehe told RTL television that giving the job to a German was "highly appropriate, and to ask for more would not be appropriate".

The German government on Wednesday approved the assignment of up to 3,300 soldiers to SFOR. Acccepting a joint proposal by Ruehe and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, the cabinet agreed Germany could pledge ground, air and naval units for the force.
